prompt: Revision history should protect users from save conflicts. When the same note is edited from two windows, a stale save must not silently overwrite newer content. Use the note's revision history to detect this. Implement, with these exact Rust signatures and module paths (crate name `vaultdesk`): in module `vaultdesk::commands::notes`, `pub fn save_note_with_revision(store: &mut RevisionStore, payload: SaveNotePayload) -> <result>` and a `pub struct SaveNotePayload` with public fields `path: String`, `content: String`, `expected_revision: u64`, and `overwrite: bool`. The returned result must expose public fields `ok: bool`, `conflict: bool`, `revision: u64` (the new revision id on an accepted save), and `current_revision: u64` (the note's actual current revision). A save whose `expected_revision` does not equal the note's current revision id must be rejected as a conflict (`ok` false, `conflict` true) and must not record anything, leaving the stored content and current revision unchanged, unless `overwrite` is true. An accepted save records a new revision (via the Stage 1 RevisionStore) and returns its new `revision`. A rejected save must set `current_revision` to the note's actual current revision so the client can re-sync. The existing Stage 1 revision-history functions, struct, paths and signatures (`vaultdesk::commands::revisions::{save_note_revision, list_note_revisions, get_note_revision}`, `vaultdesk::fs::revision_store::RevisionStore`) must keep working unchanged.
issue_title: Revision history should protect users from save conflicts.
issue_body: Revision history should protect users from save conflicts. When the same note is edited from two windows, a stale save must not silently overwrite newer content. Use the note's revision history to detect this. Implement, with these exact Rust signatures and module paths (crate name `vaultdesk`): in module `vaultdesk::commands::notes`, `pub fn save_note_with_revision(store: &mut RevisionStore, payload: SaveNotePayload) -> <result>` and a `pub struct SaveNotePayload` with public fields `path: String`, `content: String`, `expected_revision: u64`, and `overwrite: bool`. The returned result must expose public fields `ok: bool`, `conflict: bool`, `revision: u64` (the new revision id on an accepted save), and `current_revision: u64` (the note's actual current revision). A save whose `expected_revision` does not equal the note's current revision id must be rejected as a conflict (`ok` false, `conflict` true) and must not record anything, leaving the stored content and current revision unchanged, unless `overwrite` is true. An accepted save records a new revision (via the Stage 1 RevisionStore) and returns its new `revision`. A rejected save must set `current_revision` to the note's actual current revision so the client can re-sync. The existing Stage 1 revision-history functions, struct, paths and signatures (`vaultdesk::commands::revisions::{save_note_revision, list_note_revisions, get_note_revision}`, `vaultdesk::fs::revision_store::RevisionStore`) must keep working unchanged.
expected_behavior: A save whose expectedRevision equals the note's current revision is accepted and records a new revision.
A stale save with overwrite false is rejected as a conflict and records nothing.
A stale save with overwrite true is accepted and records a new revision.
A rejected save reports the note's actual current revision and leaves the stored content unchanged.
The Stage 1 revision-history functions continue to behave exactly as before.
expected_failure_summary: save_note_with_revision records every save unconditionally and never inspects expectedRevision, so a stale save from a second window always overwrites the newer content, never reports a conflict, and never returns the note's actual current revision.
task_author_notes: Stage 2 of the vaultdesk_revision_conflicts group. Runs on the agent's Stage 1 candidate (revision history). Reference adds conflict detection to save_note_with_revision (commands/notes.rs) on top of the Stage 1 RevisionStore: reject when expectedRevision != current_revision_id and overwrite is false (record nothing, report current id), otherwise record a new revision. Extension friction is high when Stage 1 modelled history as an append-only opaque blob with no addressable current revision; low when Stage 1 exposed a current revision id. Stage 2 is the designated long-output task: tests_visible/run_revision_stress.py emits a deterministic 50-300 KB save/conflict simulation.
